item.title: What Zero False Alarms Taught Me About Physics-Informed ML
item.description: In April 2025, a combined sewer in Peel Region, Ontario overflowed. We caught it 7 hours and 40 minutes before it happened. That number — 7h40m — is the kind of thing you spend years working toward and then, when it finally appears in a log, you stare at it for longer than you should. The Problem With Pure ML on Physical Systems Water utility telemetry is hostile data. Sensors fail mid-storm.

item.title: Why I'm Betting My Next Five Years on Go
item.description: There’s a kind of professional decision that looks small from the outside but reshapes everything downstream. For me, the decision to commit to Go as my primary language over the next five years is one of those. I’ve been writing software for 15 years. I started in C++ doing IEC 61850 protocol implementations and native desktop GIS tooling. Moved through Scala for ML infrastructure. Built time-series pipelines in Python. And somewhere in the middle of all of that, I noticed that the languages I enjoyed most were the ones that got out of my way.

item.title: About
item.description: CTO & Co-founder, Infinitii AI · Gdańsk, Poland I build ML systems for municipal water utilities. Specifically: physics-informed time-series models that predict sewer overflow events before they happen, giving operations teams hours of lead time instead of seconds of alarm. Our core production system is Lark, a Go library validated on Peel Region, Ontario — 13 storms, zero false alarms, with one real overflow caught 7 hours and 40 minutes before it occurred.

item.title: Speaking
item.description: I speak on physics-informed ML, MLOps for infrastructure, and time-series modeling in domains where the data is messy and the consequences are real. Past Talks PyData Global — Time-series anomaly detection in water utility telemetry PyCon Lithuania — Domain knowledge as a regularizer: lessons from sewer overflow prediction ML Conference Berlin — Physics-informed models: encoding what you know before you learn Current Pitches I’m actively submitting to events in 2025–2026.
